audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2, Level 3, First item and 2+ items are marked Jax in the full layer but carry Akshan-favoured boilerplate. Separately, the chart itself is internally contradicted: win[1] and win[2] give Jax levels 2 and 3, while spikes[0] calls 2-3 "your one clean trading window all lane" and whys[1] calls it "your cleanest trades all game".
audit.why: The stage text and the stage side cannot both be right. I fixed the boilerplate, but I did not flip levels 2-3, because the case is genuinely two-sided — Empower is 7s at rank 1 and Relentless Assault ramps his attack speed, so Jax can win a stand-and-trade at 2 even before Counter Strike exists. That call needs a human, so it is in questionsForUser rather than guessed at.
audit.corrected: The four boilerplate stages now argue for their own side (Empower's 7s at 2, Counter Strike at 3, Grandmaster-at-Arms resists at first item, his combo at two). The levels 2-3 side conflict is flagged, not silently resolved.

audit.whatIsWrong: Jax's ultimate is called "Grandmaster's Might" in three places — spikes[1], the mid text and whys[4].
audit.why: The ability is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Grandmaster's Might was its old name and is no longer what the player sees on the ability bar. The description also carries a second half the page never mentions: every third consecutive attack deals bonus magic damage, which is part of why his level-6 spike is a takeover and not just a defensive button.
audit.corrected: The real name is used in all three places, and the third-attack magic damage is stated alongside the armour and magic resist so the spike reads as the threat it is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is the ability the entire page is built around and its cooldown is never given once, in either layer. dosFull[2] describes a spent Counter Strike only as "the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee" with no duration.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17/15/13/11/9s — the longest cooldown in Jax's kit by a wide margin and the single number that tells you when to trade. Against Akshan it matters twice over, because Riot's description is that it "dodge[s] all incoming attacks" — that is Dirty Fighting's second shot and every auto in your pattern, i.e. most of your damage — and then stuns. Leap Strike at 8s and Empower at 7s are the short cooldowns that make his approach constant by comparison.
audit.corrected: 17s at rank 1 is now stated in the win condition, the 4-5 stage, the cooldown block, both do's, the interactions report and the mid and wants text, with Leap Strike's 8s and Empower's 7s given as the contrast.

edits.after: Short trades, disciplined swings, and the execute when his kit is down. Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 — schedule every pattern around that gap.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your best stretch — E (Heroic Swing) needs terrain to swing off, but at range it doubles as poke and disengage, and you can keep Jax at Avengerang distance where his Q-leap and Counter Strike stun can't reach you. But the instant he hits 6, respect his R: Grandmaster's Might piles armor and MR on him for the fight, so Comeuppance's missing-health scaling pays out far less than the math promises and your lethality autos bounce off the resists. Take the free poke, but never commit an all-in into a Jax who can E-dodge your burst and ult to survive what lands.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your best stretch — E (Heroic Swing) needs terrain to swing off, but at range it doubles as poke and disengage, and you can keep Jax at Avengerang distance where his 8s Leap Strike can't reach you. But the instant he hits 6, respect his R: Grandmaster-at-Arms piles armor and MR on him for the fight and makes every third attack deal bonus magic damage, so Comeuppance's missing-health scaling pays out far less than the math promises. Take the free poke, but never all-in a Jax who can dodge your burst with a 17s Counter Strike and ult through what lands.

notes: The _missing file claims 'Your Going Rogue (W), Heroic Swing (E) shuts off Jax's Leap Strike, Empower — hold it for the engage'. That rule misfired: neither Going Rogue nor Heroic Swing applies grounding or any effect that denies a dash, and the kit files confirm Akshan has no grounding flag anywhere. Nothing was written from it. Note also that Counter Strike dodging 'all incoming attacks' means it eats the Dirty Fighting second shot as well as your autos, which is a larger share of Akshan's damage than of most marksmen's.
